claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 15 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 15 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment by getting the first question for you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help you with your Child Benefit eligibility, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**First, let me ask about your child's age:**

Could you tell me:
1. **How old is your child?** (or if you have multiple children, their ages)
2. **What are their names?** (I'll need this for the final assessment)

This will help me understand which eligibility rules apply to your situation. The key age categories are:
- **Under 16** - Different rules apply
- **16-19** - Need to check if they're in education or training
- **20 or over** - Different eligibility rules

What are the ages and names of the child/children you're claiming for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello, yes I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and would like to know if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who is 15 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have one child, **Alex, who is 15 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, let me continue with the next check in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Since Alex is under 16, most children in this age group are eligible. Now I need to check a few more conditions.

**Question 1:** Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?

(Generally, children under 16 who work a small amount of part-time work are still eligible, but if they're working 24 hours or more per week, different rules apply.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's still at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's helpful information. Since Alex doesn't work at all, that condition is met. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now let me check the next condition:

**Question 2:** Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in their own right:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(In other words, is he not claiming any of these benefits himself?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now let me check about apprenticeships:

**Question 3:** Is Alex in an apprenticeship?

For context, here are the regional rules:
- **England:** All types of apprenticeships (Intermediate, Advanced, Higher, Degree) disqualify
- **Scotland:** Modern Apprenticeships disqualify
- **Wales:** Foundation Apprenticeships are **approved** (eligible), but other types disqualify

Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship, or is he just at school?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's just at school doing his GCSEs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is just at school and not in any apprenticeship, let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check your residency status. This is an important eligibility requirement.

**Question 4:** Which of the following best describes your residency situation? (You only need to meet ONE of these):

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most straightforward path
2. **You have settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. **You have pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme AND are:
   - Working and earning/expecting to earn above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - Actively seeking work, OR
   - Have sufficient resources to support yourself and your family, OR
   - Studying with sufficient resources, OR
   - A family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside
4. **You're a Crown servant** living abroad or in certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex. Responsibility can mean one of the following (you only need ONE):

**Question 5:** Which of these applies to you?

1. **You live with Alex** - Do you live with him?
2. **You contribute to his upkeep** - For example, you pay for his food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, or other care needs
3. **You pay maintenance** - Are you paying maintenance towards Alex under a court order or agreement?

How are you responsible for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - you live with Alex, so you meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check something important about other claimants:

**Question 6:** Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there any dispute about who should claim?

In other words:
- Are you the only person claiming/intending to claim Child Benefit for Alex?
- Or is there another person (like the other parent) who is also claiming or wants to claim for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! So you're the only claimant for Alex. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now let me check Alex's living situation:

**Question 7:** Where does Alex normally live?

- **At home with you** (normal living situation)
- **In hospital** (long-term admission)
- **In local authority care** (looked after by the council)
- **Fostered** (with foster carers)

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives at home with me - just a normal living situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex lives at home with you in a normal situation. Let me continue to the final checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost there. Just one final check:

**Question 8:** Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?

In other words, are you covering Alex's living costs yourself (food, housing, etc.) without the council paying for it?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I cover all of Alex's costs myself. The council isn't paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful! That's all the information I need. Let me now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me record your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT**

Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

---

### **Summary of Your Situation:**

✓ Alex is 15 years old (under 16)  
✓ Alex is not working full-time (at school doing GCSEs)  
✓ Alex is not receiving ESA or Universal Credit  
✓ Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship  
✓ You live in the UK (Manchester)  
✓ You live with Alex and are responsible for them  
✓ No one else is claiming for Alex  
✓ Alex lives at home normally  
✓ The council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation  

**You meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.**

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post using form CH2**
2. **Gather these documents:**
   - Proof of your identity (e.g., passport, driving licence)
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Proof of your address

3. **Important note:** If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, there's a **High Income Child Benefit Charge** - you may still get Child Benefit, but you could owe tax on it. You can avoid this by choosing not to receive payments, but you should still register as it protects your National Insurance record.

4. **Payment schedule:** Once approved, Child Benefit is usually paid every 4 weeks directly into your bank account.

For more details, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

All eligibility criteria are satisfied.
